subLocations.name: The Wide
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Upper City]] of [[Baldur's Gate]] that served as a vast open-air marketplace and plaza.

subLocations.name: Citadel Streets
subLocations.lore: A small and rather segregated district located on the north side of the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Manorborn
subLocations.lore: One of the four districts that composed the [[Upper City]], home to the richest members of the Baldurian [[patriar]], nearly every member of the [[Parliament of Peers]] resided in the district.

subLocations.name: Temples District
subLocations.lore: The largest and perhaps the oldest and most important region in the entirety of the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Seatower
subLocations.lore: One of the largest districts of [[Baldur's Gate]], located on the northern shore of the [[River Chionthar]] and housed the western docks of [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Bloomridge
subLocations.lore: A wealthy district within the [[Lower City]], south of the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]], into which it was partially built via great feats of engineering, both structural and [[arcane]].

subLocations.name: The Steeps
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Lower City]] between the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]] and the eastern side of [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Heapside
subLocations.lore: A large district in the [[Lower City]], that gained its name following the [[Tax Revolts]] of the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Eastway
subLocations.lore: One of the larger districts of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Brampton
subLocations.lore: A district in south-eastern Baldur's Gate, noteworthy in that passage through it, was required to reach the [[Outer City]] district of [[Tumbledown]].

subLocations.name: Blackgate
subLocations.lore: The region that served as a waiting area for merchants and caravaneers moving their goods along the [[Trade Way]]. They were forced to stable their pack animals in Blackgate, while their products were transferred to another conveyance while moving through the city.

subLocations.name: Stonyeyes
subLocations.lore: The neighborhood that was home to a large community of [[half-orc]]s, many of whom worked as porters, helped in transporting goods to and from caravans coming to [[Baldur's Gate]], as their pack animals were not allowed within the city walls.

subLocations.name: Little Calimshan
subLocations.lore: A rowdy and chaotic walled district in the [[Outer City]], distinct in its design and atmosphere that evoked its namesake realm of [[Calimshan]].

subLocations.name: Norchapel
subLocations.lore: An [[Outer City]] neighborhood, home to many laborers and criminal gangs.

subLocations.name: Whitkeep
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Outer City]],  home to a sizable community of [[gnome]]s, many of whom worked as [[tin]]smiths within the city.

subLocations.name: Sow's Foot
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Outer City]] – the easternmost neighborhood located outside of the city walls, nestled in between [[Twin Songs]] and [[Whitkeep]].

subLocations.name: Twin Songs
subLocations.lore: A district of the [[Outer City]] located on the northern side of the [[Wyrm's Crossing]] bridge that was an expansive collection of temples and shrines dedicated to nearly every deity including dark and malevolent deities.

subLocations.name: Tumbledown
subLocations.lore: A lone and perpetually foggy district located within the [[Outer City]], the location of the [[Cliffside Cemetery]].

subLocations.name: Rivington
subLocations.lore: The southernmost district of [[Baldur's Gate]] and the only region of the [[Outer City]] located on the southern shore of the [[River Chionthar]].

subLocations.name: Wyrm's Crossing
subLocations.lore: This district was comprised of two massively-tall stone bridges that spanned the length of the [[River Chionthar]].

subLocations.name: Hissing Stones
subLocations.lore: A bathhouse and a local landmark with a sterling reputation as the city's safest and most confidential meeting area among the various Baldurian power groups.

subLocations.name: Fury of the Fist
subLocations.lore: A statue located outside the [[Seatower of Balduran]], west of the drawbridge, vandalized by [[thieves]] in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Distant Shores
subLocations.lore: A merchant of imported goods and products native to [[Chult]].

subLocations.name: Harbreeze Bakery
subLocations.lore: A bakery offered such favorite delicacies as [[cinnamon]] [[cookie]]s and full loaves of [[sugarbread]] highlighted by the flavors of foreign [[tea]]s and [[spice]]s.

subLocations.name: Felogyr's Fireworks
subLocations.lore: A four-story stone shop on [[Bindle Street]] that traded in [[fireworks]], [[torch]]es, [[candle]] wicks, and other lesser alchemical items, and as of the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]], the sole producer of [[smokepowder]] within [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Beloved Ranger
subLocations.lore: A large statue that portrayed a larger-than-life depiction of the [[Rashemaar]] [[ranger]] [[Minsc]] and his rodent companion, both were revealed to be [[petrified]] heroes, released in the 1480s [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Counting House
subLocations.lore: The center of trade and business in [[Baldur's Gate]], serving as both a bank and establishment that facilitated the exchange of various currencies.

subLocations.name: Sorcerous Sundries
subLocations.lore: A magic shop on [[Stormshore Street]] in the [[Heapside]] district.

subLocations.name: Eastway Expeditions
subLocations.lore: A shop that specialized in selling equipment to those who sought exploration or adventure, particularly those ''en route'' to the [[Chultan Peninsula]].

subLocations.name: Candulhallow's Funeral Arrangements
subLocations.lore: A city-sponsored business that specialized in the transportation and occasionally sale of corpses to cemeteries or temples.

subLocations.name: Insight Park
subLocations.lore: A public park that was magically created during the mid–15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Danthelon's Dancing Axe
subLocations.lore: A general store that sold good quality secondhand wares, from pots and pans to [[rope]], [[armor]], and [[weapons]].

subLocations.name: Hamhocks Slaughterhouse
subLocations.lore: A massive compound composed of a number of animal pens, knackeries, and butcheries, its foul stench drove away the animals of the herders and wranglers.

subLocations.name: Garynmor Stables and Menagerie
subLocations.lore: A business that specialized in the handling and care of mundane beasts of burden, as well as the exhibition of all manner of exotic and fantastical creatures.

subLocations.name: The Oasis
subLocations.lore: A theater known for the rich production values of its show and the lavish spectacles it was capable of exhibiting in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Balduran Looks Out to Sea
subLocations.lore: A statue that depicted the famous explorer [[Balduran]], after whom the city was named.

subLocations.name: Cliffside Cemetery
subLocations.lore: The largest graveyard in [[Baldur's Gate]], a sprawling plot of land turned cemetery around the  [[Szarr]] family tombs and the [[Szarr Mansion]].

subLocations.name: River Chionthar
subLocations.lore: A large river that ran through the [[Western Heartlands]].

subLocations.name: Gray Harbor
subLocations.lore: The harbor of [[Baldur's Gate]] on [[River Chionthar]], one of the busiest and deepest natural harbors in [[Faerûn]].

subLocations.name: Calim Jewel Emporium
subLocations.lore: Shop and home to the most well-regarded [[Baldurian]] jeweler of the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]] and a forum for local agents of the criminal organization known as [[the Guild]].

subLocations.name: Seaserpent Tamed by Umberlee
subLocations.lore: A statue dedicated to [[Umberlee]], the Bitch Queen, that rose out of the [[Gray Harbor]] waters.

subLocations.name: Six Wise Machinists
subLocations.lore: A statue that was vandalized in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Faithful Shopkeeper Meets the Honest Trader
subLocations.lore: A statue vandalized by thieves in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: The Queen's Favor
subLocations.lore: A statue landmark of note.

subLocations.name: Candlekeep Chandlery
subLocations.lore: A shop that sold beautifying products and [[candle]]s, both mundane and magical in nature.

subLocations.name: Lucky Aello's Discount Store
subLocations.lore: A store that sold heavily marked-down goods that ranged from [[potion]]s of reliable quality to ''[[curse]]d'' [[weapon]]s and [[scroll]]s of magic protection.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Maltz's Weapon Shop
subLocations.lore: A merchant who dealt in mandate weapons, ran by [[Maltz]] in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]], located just to the northwest of the [[Elfsong Tavern]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Well-Adjusted Al's General Store
subLocations.lore: The general store located to the west of the [[Low Lantern]]; it traded in mundane goods and [[weapon]]s and run by eccentric [[Well-Adjusted Al]] in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Alabaster Stonecrafts
subLocations.lore: An open-air stonemason's workshop run by twin [[dwarf|dwarven]] siblings in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Statue of Balduran
subLocations.lore: A monolithic statue of [[Balduran]], looming over the ships entering the [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Rivington General
subLocations.lore: A smithy that dealt in [[weapon]]s and [[armor]], run by [[Gyldro Angleiron]] after [[1477 DR]]. Its shop area was a building to the north, with the southern connected structure being the workshop and the proprietor's home.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Bonecloak's Apothecary
subLocations.lore: A [[potion]] brewer's shop run by [[Derryth Bonecloak]] and [[Baelen Bonecloak]] ''circa'' [[1492 DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Bloomridge Park
subLocations.lore: A small public park nestled at the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]], east of the [[Manor Gate]].{{approx}}
